title: Dallas, David Jones's band, Danny Barker and Luis Russell
summary: Lee summarizes his moves: Dallas, the David Jones band and recording, then New York in 1929 with Luis Russell, and Chicago with Dave Payton.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, I played the entertainers quite a while, about two years. I leaves and go to Dallas, Texas. And Professor Cook, Professor Cook, who's a dance, dancing man, Charleston man. We go there and we take the band, we made a nice little round there. And I come on back to New Orleans and I went to Wake to see what bands I went to Wake with. I think I made up a band of my own. I went back to the La Vida Club and I leave there and go on that story with David Jones' band. David Jones was the greatest, one of the finest musicians that I've worked with in my life. Oh, that man was a great. He could play sax cornet. He could play anything as good as anybody. So, that story, how they eat. That's why I went to the Test Story Band. I started, we recorded that band. I went and got my boy that played clarinet with me, Sidney Atkins. That played with me.
And you had another clarinet in there before or not?

Yeah, with clarinet. There was a little, well, they weren't much clarinet players. The alto saxophone players played a little clarinet. Wiggles they called it. Poirier. Poirier to hell. So, we go to Wake. We go to Wake in Estoria. And so, I take a little Danny Barker. I had a band, put him in. He never played music. I brought him music well. We go up there and I went to Wake for Beansy. And I stayed up there and clean until I joined Lou Russell's band, New York. Saratoga Club. 29, I leave New Orleans and go to New York City with Russell's band. Russell's band, I come back here and went with Dave Payton's band, Regal Theater. Dave Payton's band, I've been on my own around Chicago ever since.
